prompt.content:
You are generating synthetic enterprise support ticket text for a dataset used to train and evaluate support-case classification systems. For each case in the input JSON array, write a realistic support ticket TITLE and DESCRIPTION as the customer would write it — not as an engineer would describe the internal diagnosis.

Vary sentence structure, technical sophistication, length, clarity, and tone across cases. Some customers are precise; some are rambling, use shorthand, misspell things, or bury the important detail in the third sentence. Never state the internal root cause, resolution type, issue subcategory, or team name verbatim — those are back-office labels the customer has never seen. Only reference the symptoms, environment, impact, and (if given) the customer's own theory/misdiagnosis.

Follow the "narrative_instruction" field for each case exactly.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object: {"cases": [{"i": <int>, "title": "...", "description": "..."}, ...]} covering every case index in the input, in any order.

[{'i': 0, 'product_customer_sees': 'SSO Integration Module', 'environment': 'production', 'region': 'EU-Central', 'symptoms_observed': ['account locked out', 'session expired unexpectedly'], 'reported_business_impact': 'moderate', 'reported_affected_users': 30, 'narrative_instruction': 'Write a clear, reasonably well-organized ticket. The customer describes what they observed accurately and with enough detail to act on.'}]

response:
{"cases": [{"i": 0, "title": "SSO Integration Module causing unexpected session expirations and account lockouts for EU users", "description": "Hello,

We are experiencing significant issues with the SSO Integration Module in our production environment (EU-Central region) since earlier this morning.

Approximately 30 users are reporting that their sessions are expiring much faster than usual, sometimes right after they log in. When they try to refresh or log back in, they are getting locked out of their accounts entirely. This is happening intermittently but is currently preventing our EU-based teams from accessing the platform.

We have verified that these users' credentials are correct and that the issue is not related to their local browsers or network. It seems strictly tied to the SSO session management. Please investigate why valid sessions are being terminated prematurely and what triggers the subsequent lockouts."}]}
